title: Finish before starting more
hook: Three started tasks are not three finished tasks.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Compare serial completion to round-robin partial progress.

objective: Compare serial completion to round-robin partial progress.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Three started tasks are not three finished tasks. Which completes the first five-minute job at minute five? Correct option: One job to completion. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: In the whole-job view each bar is one job run to completion. Slicing the same 30 minutes of work into 5-minute turns delays the first completion from minute 5 to minute 15; starting and finishing are different counts.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. W-367 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): Opening view (Run queue, step 1) is the 5-minute round-robin of order three, two, one: ends 30, 25, 15, first completion 15 (roundRobinQueue). "Try target" whole-job order one, two, three: first completion 5. "Swap first" (two, three, one) whole-job: first completion 10. Total 5+10+15=30 minutes. Fixture test "round-robin activity does not imply the first task is complete". Fixed after FC LH-1 dispute; awaiting fact-checker re-check. FC LH-4 (2026-10-14, fact-checker, W-380): DISPUTED: the stage numbers are right (round-robin of order three, two, one ends 30, 25, 15, first completion 15; whole-job one, two, three first completion 5), but the causal sentence is false: slicing does not cause the 5 → 15 change. Same order, sliced or whole: three, two, one gives first completion 15 both ways; one, two, three gives 5 both ways (queueResult and roundRobinQueue in node). The difference is the job order, because job one (5 min) fits in a single 5-minute turn. Fix (builder and cm decide): either compare the same order in both views with a first job longer than one turn (e.g. three 10-minute jobs: whole-job 10 vs round-robin 20, as the recall does), or reword to name the order ("Running the 5-minute job first finishes it at minute 5; the opening view starts with the 15-minute job"). Record: company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH4-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: order. Exercise only; no measured productivity gain. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, work-in-process-limit fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: cumulative execution with stated setup cost; waiting is sum of start times; late means finish>due; dependency breach means predecessor is later in order. For the initial schedule, every unfinished task receives one five-minute slice per round; displayed rectangles are actual execution slices. First completion is min of completion times. The alternate schedule runs whole jobs serially. No switching overhead or empirical efficiency is assumed. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Rotating, the first task gets its second 5 minutes at 15–20, so it completes at 20, not 10.

recall.question: Three 10-minute tasks. You either finish them one by one, or rotate 5 minutes on each. When is the first task done in each plan?
options: Minute 10 one by one; minute 20 rotating
Minute 10 one by one; minute 10 rotating
Minute 10 one by one; minute 5 rotating
recall.why: Rotating, the first task gets its second 5 minutes at 15–20, so it completes at 20, not 10.
